description: The mod 9 Preimage Sieve exploits that integers congruent to 2, 4, 5, or 8 mod 9 lie on the trajectory of a smaller integer — they are preimages under T or T^3. This eliminates 4/9 (~44.4%) of all candidates from verification. The sieve generalizes to mod 3^k but with diminishing returns. Angeltveit implements this via bitwise AND of precomputed bitvectors, avoiding expensive modular arithmetic on the GPU.
mathematical_formalization: T(2n+1) = 3n+2, so any m ≡ 2 mod 3 is T(some smaller n). T^3(8n+3) = 9n+4, so any m ≡ 4 mod 9 is T^3(some smaller n). Combined: {n : n mod 9 ∈ {0,1,3,6,7}} survive. Survival rate = 5/9 ≈ 55.6%.
analogical_connections: Syndrome decoding in error-correcting codes — use residue to identify correctable patterns
Polyphase filter banks in signal processing — decompose signal by residue modulo decimation factor
Chinese Remainder Theorem reconstruction — combine local residue information for global inference
implementation_hypothesis: Precompute 9 bitvectors of length 2^A (A=10), one per mod-9 class of the starting value. For each output of the recursive step, compute n mod 9 once, select the appropriate bitvector, and AND it with the lookahead bitvector. This reduces mod-9 overhead from O(2^A) to O(1) per residue class.
experiment_seed: Compare runtime of naive mod-9 check (integer division per candidate) vs. bitvector AND approach on GPU for 10^12 candidates. Measure throughput in candidates/second. Test extending to mod-27 and mod-81 to quantify diminishing returns.
